Introduction:
This script is dedicated to visualizing processed data from **1DP_06_library_qc.Rmd**. The processed data are represented using **Line and Density plots** to illustrate library qualities.

```{r}
library(ggplot2)
library(patchwork)
library(tidyr) # For data reshaping
plots <- list()
col_list <- list()
orders <- list()
source("0F_general_functions.R", local = F, echo = F, print.eval = F)
source("0F_colours_orders.R", local = F, echo = F, print.eval = F)
#Read table with gene symbols end IDs
gene_symbol <- read.table("data/Smartseq3xpress.gene_names.txt", header = TRUE)
```

```{r Load data}
# Load the master coverage data
data <- read.table("ws/1DP_07_Combined_GeneBody_Coverage.txt", 
                          header = TRUE, 
                          sep = "\t", 
                          check.names = FALSE)

# Verify the first few rows and column names
head(data)
```

```{r Scaled data}
# 1. Create a copy of your data frame to hold the normalized results
normalized_data <- data

# 2. Loop through all columns except the first one (which is 'Percentile')
# We use colnames(master_data)[-1] to skip the X-axis
for (sample_name in colnames(data)[-1]) {
  
  # Get the raw values for the current sample
  raw_vals <- data[[sample_name]]
  
  # Calculate the maximum value for this sample
  max_val <- max(raw_vals, na.rm = TRUE)
  
  # Perform normalization: divide each point by the maximum
  # This ensures the peak of every curve is exactly 1.0
  normalized_data[[sample_name]] <- raw_vals / max_val
}

# 3. View the first few rows of the normalized table
head(normalized_data)
```

```{r}
# 1. Get all available sample names (excluding 'Percentile')
all_samples <- colnames(normalized_data)[-1]

# 2. Create the Prefiltered List
filtered_groups <- list(
  Spikes_nonTagged = all_samples[grepl("Spikes_nonTagged", all_samples)],
  Spikes_Tagged    = all_samples[grepl("Spikes_Tagged", all_samples)],
  nonTagged        = all_samples[grepl("nonTagged", all_samples) & !grepl("Spikes", all_samples)],
  OnlyTagged       = all_samples[grepl("OnlyTagged", all_samples)]
)

# 3. Verify the lists (you will see 3 files in each group)
print(filtered_groups)
```
```{r}
# Extract the colors from your list
# Based on your script: col_list[["Cond_preparation"]]
current_colors <- col_list[["Cond_preparation"]]

# Define the order in the legend
legend_order <- c("LiveCells", "LiveNuclei","FixedNuclei")

# Define the special titles for each category
special_titles <- c(
  "Spikes_nonTagged" = "Spike-ins (internal reads)",
  "Spikes_Tagged"    = "Spike-ins (UMI-tagged reads)",
  "nonTagged"        = "Transcriptome (internal reads)",
  "OnlyTagged"       = "Transcriptome (UMI-tagged reads)"
)

# Loop through your filtered groups
for (grp_name in names(filtered_groups)) {
  
  # Get column names for this group (e.g., FixedNuclei_nonTagged_bam, etc.)
  cols <- filtered_groups[[grp_name]]
  
  if (length(cols) > 0) {
    # Prepare the data: Filter and Pivot to Long Format
    plot_df <- normalized_data[, c("Percentile", cols)]
    plot_df_long <- pivot_longer(plot_df, cols = -Percentile, 
                                 names_to = "Sample", values_to = "Coverage")
    
    # Assign the Condition label based on the column name keywords
    plot_df_long$Condition <- NA
    plot_df_long$Condition[grepl("LiveCells", plot_df_long$Sample)] <- "LiveCells"
    plot_df_long$Condition[grepl("LiveNuclei", plot_df_long$Sample)] <- "LiveNuclei"
    plot_df_long$Condition[grepl("FixedNuclei", plot_df_long$Sample)] <- "FixedNuclei"
    
    #Convert Condition to a factor with specific levels
    plot_df_long$Condition <- factor(plot_df_long$Condition, levels = legend_order)
    
    # Create the ggplot
    p <- ggplot(plot_df_long, aes(x = Percentile, y = Coverage, color = Condition)) +
      geom_line(linewidth = 0.6) +
      scale_color_manual(values = current_colors) + # Uses your col_list values
      scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 1.1), breaks = seq(0, 1, 0.5)) +
      labs(title = special_titles[grp_name], x = "Gene body percentile (5'->3')", y = "Scaled coverage") +
      theme_mk_title +
      remove_grid+
      theme(legend.position = "none")
    
    plots[[grp_name]] <- p
  }
}

# 3. Create the Final Patchwork Object
# (A + B) / (C + D) with a collected legend at the bottom
final_integrity_plot <- (plots[["OnlyTagged"]] + plots[["nonTagged"]] )/ 
                         (plots[["Spikes_Tagged"]] +plots[["Spikes_nonTagged"]])+ 
                        plot_layout(guides = 'collect') & 
                        theme(legend.position = 'bottom')

# 4. Show the plot
final_integrity_plot
```

```{r}
layout2ndline <- "
AB
CD
"
plots[["2ndline"]] <- plots[["OnlyTagged"]] + plots[["nonTagged"]] + plots[["Spikes_Tagged"]] +plots[["Spikes_nonTagged"]] + plot_layout(guides = "collect", design = layout2ndline) &  # Collect legends from all plots
  theme(
    legend.position = "right",           
    legend.justification = "center",      
    legend.margin = margin(t = +5),      
    legend.key.size = unit(0.5, "cm"),
    legend.title = element_blank()
  ) &
  plot_annotation(
    tag_levels = list(c('A', " "),  
                      theme = theme(
                        plot.tag = element_text(size = 7, face = "plain")  # Customize tag size and appearance
                      )))

plots[["2ndline"]]

ggsave(
  filename = "results/2V_FigS04_3bias_metrics.svg",              # Name of the file
  plot = plots[["2ndline"]],          # The plot object to save
  device = "svg",                          # Specify the output format (png, pdf, svg)
  width = 16.9,                              # Width of the image
  height = 9,                              # Height of the image
  units = "cm"                            # Units for width and height 
)
```

#RNA integrity
```{r}
# Define directory and the four patterns matching your read types
data_dir <- "ws/"
patterns <- c("nonTagged", "OnlyTagged", "Spikes_nonTagged", "Spikes_Tagged")

# Initialize a master list to hold the four categories
isize_master_list <- list()

for (p in patterns) {
  # 1. Identify files matching the specific pattern
  current_files <- list.files(path = data_dir, 
                              pattern = paste0("_isizes_", p, ".txt$"), 
                              full.names = TRUE)
  
  # 2. Name the files based on the isolation protocol (e.g., FixedNuclei)
  names(current_files) <- gsub(paste0("_isizes_", p, ".txt"), "", basename(current_files))
  
  # 3. Load the numeric data into a sub-list
  isize_master_list[[p]] <- lapply(current_files, function(f) {
    scan(f, quiet = TRUE)
  })
}
```

```{r}
# Check how many protocols were loaded for each pattern
sapply(isize_master_list, length)
```

```{r}
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)

special_titles <- c(
 "Spikes_nonTagged" = "Spike-ins (internal reads)",
 "Spikes_Tagged"    = "Spike-ins (UMI-tagged reads)",
 "nonTagged"        = "Transcriptome (internal reads)",
 "OnlyTagged"       = "Transcriptome (UMI-tagged reads)"
)

# Loop for visualisation
for (cat_name in names(isize_master_list)) {
  
  # Converting a sub-list (protocols) for a given category to a single data.frame
  plot_data <- bind_rows(lapply(names(isize_master_list[[cat_name]]), function(prep_name) {
    data.frame(
      insert_size = isize_master_list[[cat_name]][[prep_name]],
      Prep = prep_name
    )
  }))
  
  # Ensure Prep is a factor to maintain standard ordering (LiveCells -> LiveNuclei -> FixedNuclei)
  plot_data$Prep <- factor(plot_data$Prep, levels = orders[["Cond_preparation"]])
  
  # Kontrola, zda jsou v kategorii nějaká data
  if (nrow(plot_data) > 0) {
    p_obj <- ggplot(plot_data, aes(x = insert_size, fill = Prep, color = Prep)) +
      geom_density(alpha = 0.1) +
      scale_fill_manual(values = col_list[["Cond_preparation"]]) +
      scale_color_manual(values = col_list[["Cond_preparation"]]) +
      xlim(0, 1000) + 
      labs(
        title = paste(special_titles[cat_name]),
        x = "Insert size (bp)",
        y = "Density"
      ) +
      theme_mk_title +
      remove_grid +
      theme(legend.title = element_blank())
    
    plots[[cat_name]] <- p_obj
    
    
  }
}
```
